prompt_en: Photograph of an unmistakably adult fictional woman inside an old railway waiting-room converted into a small lantern workshop. Use the supplied portrait solely as guidance for visible face and hair appearance: a short dark bob with wispy center-parted fringe and softly rounded cheek contours. She wears an indigo apron over a white shirt and stands beside a coat hanging from a wooden rail near the window. She matches a narrow silk ribbon to the coat button, holding the ribbon end against the button with one hand while her other hand gently draws the loose ribbon level, both forearms comfortably in front of her torso. Photograph from outside through one continuous window pane: her face and hands are visibly transmitted through clear glass, while faint reflected railway-canopy beams and an overhead wire occupy the upper and side portions of that same pane. the central facial area remains transparent and legible. Near-lens sheer saffron fabric strips blur into soft foreground bokeh along the left and lower frame edges, enclosing the sharply resolved face deeper in the scene. A small faceted prism at the extreme right edge of the camera produces a narrow peripheral refracted slice containing a displaced duplicate outline of the red indicator lamp, with a subtle spectrum fringe; the central face retains a single coherent outline. A small red indicator lamp glows behind her. An open tin of numbered tags, a partly repaired lantern, and damp window droplets make the workshop tangible. Eye-level rich layered scene. a scene-owned near object occupies a peripheral foreground region; that near object remains softer than the resolved main face; a clear opening through the foreground reveals the intended face region; overlap and softness separate foreground subject and farther setting; a visible pane edge or frame locates the glass plane between camera and subject; the subject face is seen through the pane in the transmitted scene; a restrained exterior reflection overlays a distinct region of the pane; the transmitted expression-bearing face remains readable through the layered pane; a localized peripheral region shows refracted displacement or spectral separation; the optical effect remains near a chosen image edge; the central requested facial features remain coherent and resolved; the shifted edge detail remains connected to the same scene or light source. Saffron folds form a loose aperture around her cheeks instead of crossing her eyes. Her face occupies the workshop side of rain-speckled glass while the canopy belongs to the reflected exterior. The red glow lightly catches the tin rim beneath the cooler daylight. The portrait ends just below her waist, keeping both working hands and the coat button within view.
